## Human cognitive sovereignty

Researchers retain the ability to understand, direct, question, and take responsibility for work.

What intellectual responsibility do you want to preserve in your own practice?


## Principal and agent

A human sets the objective and delegates bounded work.

The governance problem concerns both authority over choices and evidence about execution.


## Two governing principles

**Researcher control** preserves consequential human judgment.

**Radical transparency** makes work and its provenance inspectable.

::: {.source}
Paci, [With Great Powers](https://simonepaciphd.github.io/with-great-powers/)
:::


## Substantive and procedural work

| Choice or task | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Research question or method | Designated human |
| Implementation of an approved specification | Delegated, then checked |
| Interpretation or headline claim | Designated human |
| Formatting approved results | Delegated, then checked |


## Judgment inside technical work

A merge command can encode a decision about a valid match.

An exclusion rule can change a result's meaning.

Classify the consequential choice, even when it appears inside code.


## Monitoring

Keep task records, artifact provenance, verification evidence, uncertainties, and human decisions.

Use them at meaningful checkpoints to judge what happened.


## Alignment

Specify goals, constraints, permitted procedural work, and escalation points.

Corresponding checks and interventions make the rules usable.


## Escalation

A decision request identifies the choice, options, evidence, uncertainty, consequences, and responsible human.

Peer discussion and AI criticism can inform that decision.


## Proposed practice

Apply a personal governance layer to the introduction workspace.

Demonstrate one procedural delegation and one consequential question returned to the appropriate human.


## Evidence for discussion

Which decisions remain yours?

What do the records establish?

Where could a formally approved output still conceal a judgment you did not intend to delegate?
